rsonar in practice

Measuring and improving R code quality, step by step

Damien Dotta

What is rsonar?

rsonar is the R equivalent of SonarQube: it centralizes R code quality measurement into one interactive report.

Tool Role
lintr Static analysis — bugs, style, complexity
styler Code formatting
covr Test coverage
goodpractice Package best practices

SonarQube vocabulary: issues, Coverage, Quality Gate.

SQALE: quantifying technical debt

SQALE = Software Quality Assessment based on Lifecycle Expectations.

The method popularized by SonarQube — and reused by rsonar — to turn code defects into an estimated cost, expressed in minutes.

Four key concepts:

  1. Penalty per issue (minutes)
  2. Debt ratio (%)
  3. SQALE rating (A to E)
  4. How the estimated cost is calculated

The penalty per issue

Each issue has a remediation cost: the estimated time to fix it, in minutes.

Issue Default penalty
lintr error 30 min
lintr warning 10 min
Style violation 2 min
Badly formatted file (styler) 5 min
goodpractice failure 20 min
Missing coverage point 5 min / point

Total debt = the sum of these penalties.

The debt ratio

Total debt is compared to a baseline effort:

ratio = D_total / (files × 30 min)
  • D_total: sum of penalties across all issues
  • files × 30 min: estimated effort to develop the files

The quality score is derived from it:

score = 100 × (1 - min(1, ratio))

The SQALE rating (A → E)

The ratio is converted into a maintainability rating:

Ratio Rating Meaning
< 5 % A Excellent
5 – 10 % B Good
10 – 20 % C Acceptable
20 – 50 % D Poor
> 50 % E Critical

The estimated cost: the method

  1. Count the issues (errors, warnings, style, coverage, goodpractice)
  2. Sum their penalties → total debt in minutes
  3. Divide by the baseline effort → debt ratio
  4. Convert the ratio into a SQALE rating (A → E)

Baseline effort: SonarQube → lines of code × 30 min; rsonar → files × 30 min.

Example: 2 errors + 2 warnings + 5 style = 90 min, against 300 min (10 files) → ratio 30 % → rating D.

The plan: measure, improve, measure

A loop, on a single running example:

  1. Start from problematic code
  2. Measure quality with rsonar (score, rating, debt)
  3. Improve the code step by step
  4. Re-measure and watch the score go up

The starting code (version 0)

File R/analysis.R:

addcols <- function(d,a,b){
  if(nrow(d)==0){stop("empty")}
  total=d[[a]]+d[[b]]
  positive <- ifelse(total>0,T,F)
  result=list(total=total, positive=positive)
  return(result)
}

Problems: naming, spacing, = vs <-, T/F, no docs, no tests.

Step 0 — Measure the initial state

library(rsonar)
res <- sonar_analyse(".")
print(res)
-- rsonar -- Quality Report --
  Files       : 1 R
  Lint        : 8 issues (0 err / 3 warn / 5 style)
  Style       : 1 non-compliant file
  Coverage    : 0%
  Goodpractice: 3 failures

-- Technical Debt --
  SQALE: E | Score: 38% | Duration: 4.2h

Step 0 — Score, rating and hotspots

quality_score(".")   # Score: 38% | Rating: E
debt_index(res)      # Rating: E (critical debt)
sonar_hotspots(res)  # → R/analysis.R first
  • debt_index(): technical debt rating (A to E)
  • sonar_hotspots(): files to fix first
  • sonar_report(res): interactive HTML report

Step 1 — Fix style automatically

sonar_fix() is powered by air, Posit’s fast R formatter.

# Preview without changing anything
sonar_fix(".", dry_run = TRUE)

# Apply the style fixes
sonar_fix(".")

Fixes: spacing, = → <-, braces, indentation.

Step 1 — Result (version 1)

addcols <- function(d, a, b) {
  if (nrow(d) == 0) {
    stop("empty")
  }
  total <- d[[a]] + d[[b]]
  positive <- ifelse(total > 0, T, F)
  result <- list(total = total, positive = positive)
  return(result)
}

Style is fixed, but naming, complexity and docs remain.

Re-measure: Score 62% · Rating D.

Step 2 — Refactor and document

Manual improvements:

  • addcols → add_columns, d/a/b → data/col1/col2
  • ifelse(x > 0, T, F) → x > 0
  • roxygen documentation added
#' Sum two columns and flag positive rows
#'
#' @param data A data frame.
#' @param col1,col2 Column names to sum.
#' @return A list with `total` and `positive`.
add_columns <- function(data, col1, col2) {
  if (nrow(data) == 0) {
    stop("`data` must contain at least one row.")
  }
  total <- data[[col1]] + data[[col2]]
  list(total = total, positive = total > 0)
}

Re-measure: Score 78% · Rating C.

Step 3 — Add tests

tests/testthat/test-analysis.R:

test_that("add_columns sums and flags", {
  data <- data.frame(a = c(1, -2, 3), b = c(0, 5, -5))
  res <- add_columns(data, "a", "b")

  expect_equal(res$total, c(1, 3, -2))
  expect_equal(res$positive, c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE))
})

Coverage goes from 0% to 85%.

Re-measure: Score 94% · Rating A.

The progress at a glance

Step Action Score Rating Coverage
0 Starting code 38 % E 0 %
1 Auto style (sonar_fix) 62 % D 0 %
2 Refactor + docs 78 % C 0 %
3 Tests added 94 % A 85 %

Each targeted improvement raises the score and lowers the debt.

Step 4 — Block regressions (Quality Gate)

quality_gate(res,
  coverage_min    = 80,
  lint_errors_max = 0,
  rating_min      = "B",
  fail_on_error   = TRUE)

If a threshold is crossed, the CI pipeline blocks automatically.

This is the guard that prevents the rating from dropping back.

Track the evolution over time

# Compare two analyses (before / after)
sonar_diff(res_v3, res_v0)

# Save scores to plot the trend
sonar_trend(res, file = "rsonar-history.json")
  • sonar_diff(): new issues, fixed issues
  • sonar_trend(): rating evolution curve

Export results (CI)

export_junit(res, "junit-results.xml")      # GitLab/Jenkins
export_sarif(res, "results.sarif")          # GitHub Code Scanning
export_sonar_json(res, "sonar-issues.json") # SonarQube

Standard formats: JUnit XML, SARIF 2.1.0, SonarQube Generic Issue Import.

Going further: automate the fixes

sonar_fix(".", create_mr = TRUE) opens a Merge/Pull Request directly.

CI job rsonar-fix (optional manual task):

  1. Installs air (install_air())
  2. Formats all R files (sonar_fix())
  3. Opens an MR/PR with the fixes

→ No more manual reformatting: trigger, review, merge.

CI Pipeline (GitLab)

stages: [quality, autofix]

rsonar-check:
  stage: quality
  script: R -e "sonar_analyse('.'); export_junit()"

rsonar-fix:
  stage: autofix
  when: manual
  script: R -e "sonar_fix('.', create_mr = TRUE)"

Key takeaways

rsonar = measure, fix, secure:

  • Locally: quality_score() and debt_index() for instant feedback
  • In depth: sonar_analyse() + sonar_report() + sonar_hotspots()
  • Over time: sonar_diff() / sonar_trend() to watch the rating improve
  • In CI: quality_gate() + exports + sonar_fix(create_mr = TRUE)

Conclusion

The pedagogical loop:

  1. Start from problematic code
  2. Measure quality (score, rating, debt)
  3. Improve step by step (style → refactor → tests)
  4. Watch the rating climb: 38% → 62% → 78% → 94%
